content.title: Measures of Central Tendency: Mean, Median, and Mode
content.overview: This lesson covers the calculation and identification of the three primary measures of central tendency—mean, median, and mode—for small data sets and frequency tables.
learning_objectives: Calculate the arithmetic mean and weighted average of a data set.
Identify the median of a data set by ordering values and finding the middle position.
Determine the mode of a data set based on frequency.
Apply these measures to both simple lists and frequency tables.

sections.title: The Arithmetic Mean
sections.content:
The mean, often called the average, is the sum of all values in a data set divided by the total number of values (n). For a simple list, use the formula: Mean = (Sum of all values) / n. When data is presented in a frequency table, calculate the weighted average by multiplying each value by its frequency, summing those products, and dividing by the total frequency (the sum of the frequencies).

![A flowchart showing the steps to find mean, median, and mode.](https://img.justsolvely.com/followUpImage/66a18841-039e-4c25-bb08-054868720b04-1786506103498-196.webp)

sections.title: The Median
sections.content: The median is the middle value of a data set when the numbers are arranged in numerical order (ascending or descending). To find the position of the median, use the formula (n + 1) / 2. If n is odd, the median is the single middle value at that position. If n is even, the median is the arithmetic mean of the two middle values.

sections.title: The Mode
sections.content: The mode is the value that appears most frequently in a data set. A data set can have one mode (unimodal), two modes (bimodal), more than two modes (multimodal), or no mode at all if every value appears with the same frequency.

worked_examples.question: A student has the following quiz scores: 70, 70, 85, 90, 90, 90, 100. Calculate the mean, median, and mode.
worked_examples.solution: 1. Mean: Sum the scores (70 + 70 + 85 + 90 + 90 + 90 + 100 = 595). Divide by the number of scores (7): 595 / 7 = 85. 2. Median: The scores are already ordered. With n = 7, the middle position is (7 + 1) / 2 = 4th. The 4th value is 90. 3. Mode: The score 90 appears three times, which is more than any other score. Mode = 90.

worked_examples.question: Find the mean of a data set where the value 10 has a frequency of 3 and the value 20 has a frequency of 2.
worked_examples.solution: 1. Calculate the weighted sum: (10 * 3) + (20 * 2) = 30 + 40 = 70. 2. Calculate the total frequency: 3 + 2 = 5. 3. Divide the weighted sum by the total frequency: 70 / 5 = 14. The mean is 14.

common_mistakes: Calculating the median without first putting the data in numerical order.
Dividing the sum by the number of unique values instead of the total count (n) when calculating the mean.
Confusing the mode (the value itself) with its frequency (how many times it appears).
Forgetting to average the two middle numbers when the data set has an even number of values.
exam_tips: Always perform a quick 'sanity check': the mean and median must fall between the minimum and maximum values of the data set.
If a frequency table is provided, the total number of data points (n) is the sum of the frequencies, not the number of rows in the table.
On the ACT, if you are asked to find a missing value to achieve a specific mean, use the 'Sum = Mean * n' strategy.
content.recap: To master central tendency, remember: Mean is the 'balanced' average (Sum/n), Median is the 'middle' of an ordered list, and Mode is the 'most frequent' value.

knowledge_claims.content: The arithmetic mean is calculated by dividing the sum of all values by the total number of values (n).
To find the mean from a frequency table, multiply each value by its frequency, sum these products, and divide by the total frequency.
The first step in finding the median is to arrange the data values in numerical order.
If a data set has an odd number of values (n), the median is the single middle value located at the (n+1)/2 position.
If a data set has an even number of values (n), the median is the average of the two middle values.
The mode is defined as the value that occurs with the highest frequency in a data set.
A data set can have more than one mode if multiple values share the highest frequency.
The mean and median of a data set must always be greater than or equal to the minimum value and less than or equal to the maximum value.
A common error is identifying the highest frequency number as the mode, rather than the data value associated with that frequency.
In a frequency table, the total number of data points (n) is equal to the sum of all frequencies.
The median is the value that splits an ordered data set into two equal halves.
To find a missing value given a target mean, multiply the target mean by the total count (n) to find the required sum, then subtract the known values.

What is the arithmetic mean of 6, 8, 9, 7?
A) 7
B) 8
C) 7.5
D) 30
items.explanation: The sum is 30, and dividing by 4 gives 7.5.

F) 7.571428571428571
G) 7
H) 8
J) 12
items.explanation: After ordering the data, the middle value or mean of the two middle values is 7.
